article_title: Understanding the role of eye movement consistency in face recognition and autism through integrating deep neural networks and hidden Markov models
citation: Hsiao, J. H., An, J., Hui, V. K. S., Zheng, Y. & Chan, A. B. (2022). Understanding the role of eye movement consistency in face recognition and autism through integrating deep neural networks and hidden Markov models. npj Science of Learning 7:28. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-022-00139-6
title: DNN+HMM unified learning model of visual routine development in face recognition
description: The DNN+HMM is a joint learning model in which a hidden Markov model generates sequences of fixations — location and spatial-frequency scale simulating "global/local attention" — and a multi-scale CNN plus MLP learns perceptual representations from the resulting masked inputs aggregated into a visual short-term memory. The HMM provides an interpretable summary of the model's eye movement strategy that can be compared with human data via EMHMM. Trained on the LFW-a dataset with 80 models representing simulated individuals, the model accounted for the adult eyes-focused advantage and predicted that in early learning, consistency rather than pattern predicts performance.
requirements: Fixations occur within person-specific regions of interest, with constraints of human perception such as saccade noise and retinal acuity built in
constraints: The transition matrix and prior were fixed so the ROI sequence was deterministic; the model abstracts away from biological details and may not reflect nuanced individual differences among neurodiverse populations
target_learning_goals: Development of consistent visual routines (eye movement strategies) for face recognition
examples: Trained on the 100 most frequent people in LFW-a (3651 images) for 500 epochs, with partial training at 100 epochs simulating children
key_sources: Hsiao, J. H., An, J., Hui, V. K. S., Zheng, Y. & Chan, A. B. (2022). Understanding the role of eye movement consistency in face recognition and autism through integrating deep neural networks and hidden Markov models. npj Science of Learning 7:28. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-022-00139-6

article_title: A novel model of dual-network composite hydrogels for application in endoscopic submucosal dissection.
citation: Zhao Fei, Bai YunFang, Wu JunJie, Zhu ZhiHao, Mao JinLei, Aili Aikebaier, Gu HongRun, Yu ShiJie, Wang ZhiFei. (2025). A novel model of dual-network composite hydrogels for application in endoscopic submucosal dissection. BMC Gastroenterology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12876-025-04341-9
title: Dual-network composite hydrogel (DNH) gastric ESD training model
description: A 3D-printed training model combining PVA–acrylamide hydrogels with embedded hyaluronic acid–gelatin vascular networks that "replicates human gastric wall stratification (mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria)" with tunable stiffness and pressurized fluid channels simulating bleeding. Tensile testing gave Young's moduli of 0.533 MPa (full layer), 0.401 MPa (muscularis plus submucosa), and 0.168 MPa (mucosa), closely approximating reported human gastric tissue values, with conductivity near or above 0.1 S/m.
requirements: Prepared from a common mold and same batch of materials; requires an external syringe pump delivering dyed water at 25 kPa for bleeding simulation and a standard ESD knife under clinical electrosurgical settings
constraints: Mucosal layer thickness replication rated weakest (M = 4.00); lower biomechanical accuracy for layered tissue mechanics and fluid-mediated expansion than for visual–tactile fidelity
target_learners: Endoscopists in training (residents, attending physicians) learning ESD
target_learning_goals: ESD procedural skills: lesion localization, marking, submucosal injection, circumferential cutting, dissection, and hemostasis management
examples: Fifteen identical models were fabricated, each containing four lesions; only the 2 cm × 2 cm lesions were used for training and evaluation, and simulated bleeding scenarios were documented through electrocoagulation carbonation
key_sources: Zhao Fei, Bai YunFang, Wu JunJie, Zhu ZhiHao, Mao JinLei, Aili Aikebaier, Gu HongRun, Yu ShiJie, Wang ZhiFei. (2025). A novel model of dual-network composite hydrogels for application in endoscopic submucosal dissection. BMC Gastroenterology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12876-025-04341-9

article_title: A novel model of dual-network composite hydrogels for application in endoscopic submucosal dissection.
citation: Zhao Fei, Bai YunFang, Wu JunJie, Zhu ZhiHao, Mao JinLei, Aili Aikebaier, Gu HongRun, Yu ShiJie, Wang ZhiFei. (2025). A novel model of dual-network composite hydrogels for application in endoscopic submucosal dissection. BMC Gastroenterology. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12876-025-04341-9
title: Cost and reusability comparison of the DNH model with the commercial KOTOBUKI model
description: The authors compare their DNH model with the commercial KOTOBUKI model (Japan), reporting "comparable realism scores (6.0 vs. 6.1 on a 7-point scale) at substantially lower cost (USD 40 vs. USD 100) and with significantly greater reusability (> 5 training sessions vs. 1–2)". DNH preparation took approximately 4 h versus several weeks of manufacturing lead time, and the DNH model adds vascular bleeding simulation and tunable mechanical properties the authors state are absent in KOTOBUKI.
requirements: Only the KOTOBUKI commercial model was used for comparison; the comparison rests on the authors' own reported scores and costs
constraints: The comparison appears in the authors' discussion rather than as a head-to-head tested experiment; porcine tissue is noted to provide authentic mechanical feedback that the hydrogel model does not fully match
target_learners: Institutions and training programs selecting ESD simulation models, especially in resource-limited settings
target_learning_goals: Affordable, reusable simulation-based acquisition of ESD technical skills
examples: The DNH model eliminated cold-chain logistics and biosafety risks relative to ex vivo porcine stomach models while ensuring consistent batch-to-batch anatomical properties
